questions.q: WHO IS ELIGIBLE TO VOTE ABSENTEE?
questions.a: In Idaho, all voters can apply to vote absentee.

questions.q: HOW DO I REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a:
You can apply online (https://elections.sos.idaho.gov/ElectionLink/ElectionLink/BeginAbsenteeRequest.aspx) or submit an absentee ballot request form (https://sos.idaho.gov/elections/forms/absentee_ballot_request.pdf) to your County Clerk 11 days before the election.

The application must give your name, address, and mailing address to which the ballot will be forwarded. The mail-in application must be signed personally by you and be received by the County Clerk (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) no later than 11 days before the election.

questions.q: WHAT IS THE DEADLINE TO REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: You must request an absentee ballot at least 11 days before Election Day. If completing a paper request form, it must be received by your County Clerk’s office by 5pm that day.

questions.q: DO I HAVE TO REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT EACH YEAR?
questions.a: Yes, you must complete a new absentee ballot request form each calendar year. You have the option to select all the elections in that year on your request form.

questions.q: WHAT IS THE DEADLINE FOR SUBMITTING A VOTED ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: Your voted ballot must be received by your County Clerk by 8pm on Election Day for your vote to be counted.

questions.q: WHEN ARE ABSENTEE BALLOTS AVAILABLE TO VOTERS WHO HAVE REQUESTED THEM?
questions.a: Election officials start mailing out ballots to those who have requested them 45 days before the election.

questions.q: HOW DO I VOTE AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a:
When you have received your absentee ballot:

- You will receive instructions, a secrecy sleeve, and a return envelope with the ballot.
- Follow the instructions carefully. Mark your ballot using a blue or black ink pen and fill in the box or oval completely.
- Pay attention to ballot instructions and vote only for the appropriate number of candidates in each race.
- Remember to sign the outside of the return envelope. All signatures will be verified by elections staff.
- Add the required postage to the return envelope if mailing.

Return your voted ballot by mail, to a secure ballot drop box, or to your county elections office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) by 8pm on Election Day for your vote to be counted.

questions.q: HOW DO I RETURN MY VOTED ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: Return your voted ballot by mail, to a secure ballot drop box, or to your county elections office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) by 8pm on Election Day for your vote to be counted.

questions.q: CAN I TRACK MY MAILED ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: You can track your absentee ballot (https://voteidaho.gov/casting-your-ballot/#absentee-voting) status on the Secretary of State's website.

questions.q: WHAT IF I REQUESTED AN ABSENTEE BALLOT BUT WANT TO VOTE IN PERSON?
questions.a:
If you requested an absentee ballot but want to vote in person, you must surrender your absentee ballots before receiving a regular ballot. Do not mail a ballot and vote in person. For specifics, you can find your local county clerk's contact info here. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

In-person voting at the absentee elector's polling place ends at 5pm on the Friday before the election.

questions.q: HOW DO I REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT AS AN OVERSEAS OR US MILITARY VOTER?
questions.a:
Overseas citizens and U.S. military personnel can find information on how to register to vote and request an absentee ballot at the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/vote/home.htm)
